clue.text: Italian heiress left to confront heartless idea

indicators.note: a thing without its heart has lost its central letters

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
taken as written, before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A wealthy Italian woman abandoned so she can face down a thoughtless notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the two central letters of the word, leaving its first and last.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is the rich heiress of Belmont in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, set in Italy.

clue.text: What's done to criminal, I fancy, not following a particular line

indicators.note: a fancy is a whim, so the letters are twisted on a whim

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a criminal's punishment, which follows no clear course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as 'I think', but the I belongs to the fodder and 'fancy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnidirectional means acting in all directions, not along any single line.

clue.text: Follows one side turning up on cricket field before match?

definitions.text: one side turning up on cricket field before match?

blocks.clueFragment: one side turning up on cricket field before match?
blocks.note: second meaning: the face of the coin showing at the toss before play

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket captains toss a coin before a match; the side landing face up decides who bats.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them, and tails is the reverse face of a tossed coin.

clue.text: I invent an unusual solution to a snake bite?

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inventor claims a novel fix for being bitten by a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' means both an answer and a liquid medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Antivenin is serum given to counteract venom, a liquid remedy for snakebite.

clue.text: 'Isms' tend somehow to determine outlooks

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get there by some unspecified rearranging

explanation.surface: Ideologies tend in some way to shape how people view the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a fixed attitude or way of seeing things, an outlook.

clue.text: Fellow holding party has upset an iconic female

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A man throwing a party has offended a famous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iconic' hints at religious icons depicting the Virgin as well as at the pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna is the Virgin Mary, the female figure painted on countless icons.

clue.text: Measurement in a communications circuit one person has installed

indicators.note: a thing installed is set inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A reading taken from a telecoms circuit that someone has fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: The neper is a logarithmic unit for signal attenuation, used for gain and loss in telecom circuits.

clue.text: Spotted copper nabbing group in outdoor building

indicators.note: nabbing means catching hold of, so these letters wrap round the next
in places the combined letters inside the building word

blocks.note: a shed is a simple garden building
a lot is a set or group

explanation.surface: A policeman was seen catching a gang in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'seen' but means marked with blotches; 'copper' is a policeman, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Splotched means covered with irregular patches or spots.

clue.text: Ninth drought and one will be suffering — crops being this?

definitions.note: the definition is a sentence frame; scarce crops would be thin on the ground

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad state, knocked out of shape, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, 'and' joining the two parts

explanation.surface: After nine dry spells, everyone will suffer, and the harvest will be sparse.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is every letter of 'Ninth drought' and 'one'; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin on the ground is an idiom for scarce, which is what crops would be after a drought.

clue.text: Demanded to be at home with little girl and boy

blocks.note: a common boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone required to stay in the house with a young girl and a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on something is to demand it firmly; both verbs are past tense here.

clue.text: Sick-looking friend needing cover

explanation.surface: A pale, ill friend who needs a blanket over them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means pale and wan, the complexion of someone unwell.

clue.text: Notice French art showing Hell to Milton

blocks.note: an ad is a public notice
French for 'thou art' is tu es

explanation.surface: A sign pointing out French artwork that portrays the inferno as Milton saw it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old second-person form of 'are', not painting; its French equivalent is es.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton spells the underworld Ades in Paradise Lost, an archaic form of Hades.

clue.text: Lack of vitality very little to the fore in worship

indicators.note: to the fore says this small piece is placed at the front of the rest

blocks.note: the abbreviation of very, a small bit of it
enervation is a draining of energy; its V is the one that moves

explanation.surface: Listless devotion, with little energy put into prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ENERVATION and move its V from the middle to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneration is deep reverence or worship, as of a saint.

clue.text: City raised endless soldiers

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A town that mustered an unending supply of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Bremen is a major port city in north-west Germany.

clue.text: Party member in demonstration having to make haste

blocks.note: to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A political activist on a protest needing to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party member' suggests politics, but the party is the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The March Hare is a guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll's story.

clue.text: The fellow dressed in fancy state, ultimate in elegance?

definitions.text: The fellow dressed in fancy state, ultimate in elegance?

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so these letters are dressed up in a new order
one thing dressed in another is wrapped inside it
the ultimate letter of a word is its last one

explanation.surface: A man got up in an extravagant manner, the last word in stylishness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a man dressed up in style is a picture of the dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone devoted to beauty and refinement, here pictured as a dandy dressed to impress.

clue.text: Active males rest twice a year?

indicators.note: active letters are lively and moving about, ending in a new order

explanation.surface: Busy men take a break only every six months?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: semestral strictly means half-yearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Semestral means occurring every six months, hence happening twice yearly.

clue.text: Instruments in a car so complicated

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: The dashboard dials in a vehicle are so intricate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instruments' suggests car gauges, but these are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: The firs chopped? One may get a dramatic change of scenery

definitions.text: One may get a dramatic change of scenery

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Felling the fir trees would certainly transform the view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatic' is literal: a scene shifter moves sets in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene shifter is a stagehand who changes the scenery between scenes of a play.

clue.text: Male snake gets angrier

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

explanation.surface: A male serpent becomes more furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad is informal for angry, so madder means more angry.

clue.text: Sees what's wrong — nothing right in illustrations

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder

explanation.surface: Someone spots errors, finding nothing correct in the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees' looks like a verb but is the plural noun for a bishop's area. OR goes after the P of PICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese under a bishop's authority, also called a bishopric.

clue.text: Religious type is hit on the rebound

indicators.note: something on the rebound bounces back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a rap is a sharp blow

explanation.surface: A devout person is struck by a ball bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism descended from Persian refugees in India.

clue.text: Frothy stuff provided by helpless pub server

indicators.note: without help, so a word meaning help is taken away

blocks.note: a woman serving drinks at a pub; its AID (help) is removed

explanation.surface: The foam on a pint comes from a barmaid who can't cope.
explanation.definitionFit: Barm is the froth that forms on fermenting beer or malt liquor.

clue.text: Hat left out in alcove

indicators.note: out means removed, so this letter goes from the word

blocks.note: a bowler is a hard round hat
L abbreviates left; this is the letter taken away

explanation.surface: A hat abandoned in a nook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hat' could be any hat; it has to be one containing an L.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shady recess or leafy arbour, a kind of alcove.

clue.text: Not just a Parisian trade event

explanation.surface: A French exhibition that is more than a mere trade show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just' reads as 'not only', but means not fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means unjust, the opposite of just.

clue.text: Rejected everywhere, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer is spoken like the words before it

explanation.surface: Something turned down all over the place, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out a proposal is to reject or discard it.

clue.text: Slippery types falling over support, being less alert

indicators.note: something falling over ends upside down, so the word runs the other way

blocks.note: a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: Slippery customers taking a tumble on a prop because they're drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepier means drowsier, so less wide awake.

clue.text: Look to imprison a revolutionary in Texas city

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold inside, so the next letters go within

explanation.surface: Look out for a rebel jailed in a Lone Star State town.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a city in southern Texas on the Rio Grande.
